title: Cyclosporiasis outbreak in the US, by the numbers | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Some US states are facing a large and growing outbreak of diarrhea caused by cyclospora, a microscopic parasite that can contaminate fresh food or water.

Iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms has beenrecalled, and it’s likely that contaminated products have already been eaten or removed from shelves.

“We do have the outbreak under control,” US Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said Tuesday, noting the recall.

But illness can take a while to appear, and the epidemiological curve of new cases hasn’t yet slowed.

Health officials are racing to trace the details of cases in an ongoing investigation, but the parasite is notoriously difficult to find.Testing producecan be challenging, and people who are sick may be asked to remember what they ate weeks earlier to help identify a common thread.

Cases of cyclosporiasis are known to rise during spring and summer months in the US, with a typical season running from the start of May through the end of August, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. But case counts areparticularly highthis year.

Here’s what we know about the situation so far.

As of last week, the CDC has identified nearly7,000 casesof domestic cyclosporiasis this season:1,645 casesare confirmed, and about5,100 othersare undergoing further analysis to determine whether the illness was acquired in the US.

Multiple “subclusters” of cyclosporiasis cases have beeninvestigatedthis year by the US Food and Drug Administration in collaboration with the CDC and state partners.Two investigationsremain ongoing, including the particularly large multistate outbreak centered in the Midwest.

The CDC has linked1,644 casesto this specific outbreak.

However, CDC data includes only confirmed cases and hasn’t been updated since last week. Data from individual states shows much higher case counts.

The CDC has identifiedfive stateswith cases linked to the ongoing outbreak: Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia.

As of Tuesday, the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services has reported6,571 casesof cyclosporiasis during the investigation timeframe. The state health department has said that it “cannot say with certainty that every illness is linked to the same source of exposure” but that the concentrated, sharp increase in cases “strongly suggests that the vast majority of these illnesses are associated with the same outbreak.”

Ohio has reported at least1,244 cases, Indiana has reported511 cases, West Virginia has reported195 cases, and Kentucky has reported192 cases.

Michigan and Indiana update data daily on weekdays, and West Virginia reports new totals twice a week, while Ohio and Kentucky update data weekly.

“The true number of sick people in this multistate outbreak is likely higher than the number reported, and the outbreak may not be limited to the states with known illnesses,” according to an update from the CDC.

Overall,34 stateshave reported at least one domestically acquired cyclosporiasis case this season, according to the CDC.

However, some states — including California and New Jersey — have noted that the number of cases they have reported this year is in line with typical seasonal trends.

Everyone wants to know if their dinner is safe. Is cilantro safe to eat? Are tomatoes safe to eat? Is romaine lettuce safe to eat?

Health officials in Michigan said they’ve completedmore than 2,000 interviewsof people sick with cyclosporiasis. Health officials said there’s “very strong” evidence linking to outbreak toone productin particular: Shredded iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms is the likely source. That contaminated lettuce was served at some Taco Bell locations.

CDC recommends that people not eat any shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico served at Taco Bell locations in states with cases linked to the outbreak: Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia.

The FDA is working to determine whether contaminated shredded iceberg lettuce went to other places.

Taco Bell said Friday that it has removed Taylor Farms lettuce from its restaurants and its nationwide supply chain, and supplier Taylor Fresh Foods said that it’s removing all of its iceberg lettuce from central Mexico from the US market.

Taylor Farms has also recalled iceberg lettuce shipped to27 states. Some of it went to Walmart and Jack in the Box. Other shipments went to food services.

The investigation is ongoing, but no other foods have been identified to be part of this outbreak. Other foods most commonly linked to cyclospora outbreaks historically include basil, cilantro, berries and snap peas.

Federal health officials said there have been multiple investigations around cyclospora this year, some tied to the large outbreak in the Midwest, some involving single states and some involving cases not yet tied to any cluster.

Illnesses associated with the current outbreak started in mid-May, and new illnesses have started as recently as last week, according to the CDC.

It can take days – orup to two weeks– for symptoms of cyclosporiasis to appear after consuming contaminated food or water.

Symptoms include watery diarrhea, loss of appetite, weight loss, cramping, bloating and increased gas, nausea and fatigue.

People who become ill may have symptoms for weeks.

At least94 peoplehave been hospitalized in relation to the current outbreak, according to the CDC. Dozens of other cyclospora hospitalizations have been reported this year.

States specifically linked to the outbreak have reportedhundreds of cyclospora hospitalizations:

No deathshave been reported.

According to a 2023 report from the US Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety Inspection Service, the largest cyclospora outbreak in the US on record led to about1,500 casesand involved raspberries. Other large outbreaks typically haven’t surpassed 1,000 cases.

It’s likely that this currentoutbreak isthe largest cyclospora outbreak﻿in the USto date.

If all the potential cases in this season are confirmed to be related, the outbreak will also bethe largest foodborne illness outbreaksince the US began tracking them.

The total number of cyclosporiasis cases reported this year in the US is also higher than usual.

There were more than4,500 cases in 2023 ﻿and more than3,500 cases in 2024, according to federal officials. But there have already been thousands more reported this year, with at least a month left in the season.

French biotech company bioMérieux trackstrends in gastrointestinal pathogensby collecting test results from a network of laboratories.

Its data shows that the prevalence cyclospora and other parasites has surged in the US over the past month, rising fromless than 3%of tests in the second week of June tomore than 18%in the past few days.

But E. coli is still a more common culprit for stomach issues in the US right now. The surveillance data shows that the bacteria was present in more than 19% of tests.

Viruses can also cause gastrointestinal problems, and about 14% of tests in the US tested positive for these pathogens between July 19 and July 21.
